claims.evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and demonstrated through experimental data in Figures 1 and 2.

claims.claim: Expression of a second VSG directionally attenuates the ES by DOT1B-mediated histone methylation.
claims.source: We found that the expression of a second VSG alone is sufficient to silence the active VSG gene and directionally attenuate the ES by disruptor of telomeric silencing-1B (DOT1B)-mediated histone methylation.
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated through experiments comparing wild-type and DOT1B-knockout cells shown in Figure 4.

claims.claim: Three conserved expression-site-associated genes (ESAGs) serve as signal for ES attenuation.
claims.source: Three conserved expression-site-associated genes (ESAGs) appear to serve as signal for ES attenuation.
claims.evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by RNAi experiments in Figure 7 showing that depletion of ESAGs 1, 2, and 8 causes specific phenotypes.

claims.claim: Depletion of ESAGs 1, 2, and 8 causes G1-phase dormancy.
claims.source: Their depletion causes G1-phase dormancy and reversible initiation of the slender-to-stumpy differentiation pathway.
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated through RNAi experiments shown in Figure 7 and growth analysis in Figure 3.

claims.claim: Depletion of ESAGs 1, 2, and 8 causes reversible initiation of the slender-to-stumpy differentiation pathway.
claims.source: Their depletion causes G1-phase dormancy and reversible initiation of the slender-to-stumpy differentiation pathway.
claims.evidence: This is supported by PAD1 expression data in Figures 5 and 7, and the reversibility is shown in growth curves.

claims.claim: ES-attenuated slender bloodstream trypanosomes gain full developmental competence for transformation to the tsetse fly stage.
claims.source: ES-attenuated slender bloodstream trypanosomes gain full developmental competence for transformation to the tsetse fly stage.
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated through cis-aconitate treatment experiments showing EP1 expression and morphological changes in Figure 6.

claims.claim: Each olfactory sensory neuron expresses only one olfactory receptor (OR) from a family of ~1200 genes.
claims.source: In the mammalian central nervous system, each olfactory sensory neuron expresses only one olfactory receptor (OR) from a family of ∼1200 genes (Buck and Axel, 1991).
claims.evidence: This is cited from Buck and Axel, 1991.

claims.claim: Before an OR gene is expressed, all alleles are silenced and converted to heterochromatin.
claims.source: Before an OR gene is expressed, all alleles are silenced and converted to heterochromatin (Magklara et al., 2011).
claims.evidence: This is cited from Magklara et al., 2011.

claims.claim: A limiting enzymatic activity stochastically removes heterochromatin marks from one OR allele to activate it.
claims.source: A limiting enzymatic activity then stochastically removes the heterochromatin marks from one allele to activate it.
claims.evidence: This is part of the description of the OR system mechanism in the introduction.

claims.claim: The expressed OR protein mediates a feedback loop that inhibits removal of heterochromatin marks from all other alleles.
claims.source: The expressed OR protein mediates a feedback loop that inhibits removal of heterochromatin marks from all other alleles, preventing their transcription (Serizawa et al., 2003; Lyons et al., 2013).
claims.evidence: This is cited from Serizawa et al., 2003 and Lyons et al., 2013.

claims.claim: Plasmodium falciparum expresses only one out of 60 members of the var gene family.
claims.source: The malaria parasite Plasmodium falciparum, for example, expresses only one out of 60 members of the var gene family, each coding for different versions of the surface virulence factor PfEMP1 (Guizetti and Scherf, 2013).
claims.evidence: This is cited from Guizetti and Scherf, 2013.

claims.claim: The trypanosome cell surface is covered with millions of copies of VSG that form a dense layer virtually impervious to host-derived antibodies.
claims.source: In the mammalian host, the cell surface is covered with millions of copies of VSG that form a dense layer that is virtually impervious to host-derived antibodies (Cross, 1975; Engstler et al., 2007; Schwede et al., 2011).
claims.evidence: This is cited from Cross, 1975; Engstler et al., 2007; and Schwede et al., 2011.

claims.claim: VSGs are highly immunogenic and provoke a rapid and efficient immune response that diminishes the parasite population.
claims.source: VSGs are highly immunogenic and provoke a rapid and efficient immune response that diminishes the parasite population.
claims.evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the introduction.

claims.claim: Trypanosomes that have successfully switched to expression of another VSG survive immune clearance.
claims.source: Only trypanosomes that have successfully switched to expression of another, structurally similar but immunologically distinct VSG survive.
claims.evidence: This is stated as part of the antigenic variation mechanism in the introduction.

claims.claim: Trypanosomes possess several hundred VSG genes.
claims.source: Trypanosomes possess several hundred VSG genes (Berriman et al., 2005).
claims.evidence: This is cited from Berriman et al., 2005.

claims.claim: VSG genes are expressed from one of ~15 telomeric expression sites (ES).
claims.source: VSG genes are expressed from one of ∼15 telomeric expression sites (ES) but only one of these is transcribed at any given time (Hertz-Fowler et al., 2008).
claims.evidence: This is cited from Hertz-Fowler et al., 2008.

claims.claim: Chromatin remodeling plays an important role in maintaining monoallelic expression of the active ES.
claims.source: Chromatin remodeling appears to play an important role in maintaining the monoallelic expression of the active ES (Horn and McCulloch, 2010).
claims.evidence: This is cited from Horn and McCulloch, 2010.

claims.claim: Antigenic variation can result from a change in the active ES through gene conversion at the VSG locus.
claims.source: Antigenic variation can result from either a change in the active ES, usually gene conversion at the VSG locus, or by an epigenetic change that results in silencing of the active ES and transcription of a previously silent ES (in situ switch).
claims.evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about antigenic variation mechanisms.

claims.claim: Antigenic variation can result from an epigenetic change that silences the active ES and transcribes a previously silent ES (in situ switch).
claims.source: Antigenic variation can result from either a change in the active ES, usually gene conversion at the VSG locus, or by an epigenetic change that results in silencing of the active ES and transcription of a previously silent ES (in situ switch).
claims.evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about antigenic variation mechanisms.

claims.claim: No mechanism or factor has been identified that is involved in the initiation of in situ switching prior to this study.
claims.source: No mechanism or factor has been identified that is involved in the initiation of the latter.
claims.evidence: This statement establishes the novelty of the current findings.

claims.claim: The trypanosome bloodstream form ES is exclusively functional in the proliferating slender bloodstream stage.
claims.source: Consequently, the trypanosome bloodstream form ES is exclusively functional in the proliferating slender bloodstream stage of the parasite.
claims.evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about ES function during the life cycle.

claims.claim: Trypanosomes differentiate to the quiescent stumpy form in response to quorum sensing.
claims.source: In response to quorum sensing, the trypanosomes differentiate to the quiescent stumpy form.
claims.evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about trypanosome development.

claims.claim: Stumpy forms are competent for developmental transition to procyclic forms after ingestion by a tsetse fly.
claims.source: Stumpy forms are competent for the next developmental transition to procyclic forms, which occurs after ingestion by a tsetse fly (Reuner et al., 1997).
claims.evidence: This is cited from Reuner et al., 1997.

claims.claim: Developmental transition from stumpy to procyclic forms is accompanied by silencing of the active ES.
claims.source: This developmental transition is accompanied by silencing of the active ES so that allelic exclusion is lost.
claims.evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about ES behavior during development.

claims.claim: VSG121 mRNA reached 82(±1)% of wild type levels within 2 hr of tetracycline induction.
claims.source: Quantitative Northern blot analysis revealed an almost instantaneous increase of VSG121 mRNA, reaching 82(±1)% of wild type levels within 2 hr (Figure 1B).
claims.evidence: This is directly measured experimental data shown in Figure 1B.

claims.claim: Endogenous VSG221 transcripts declined with kinetics compatible with mRNA half-life following VSG121 induction.
claims.source: This was followed by a reduction of endogenous VSG221 transcripts, which declined with kinetics compatible with the mRNA half-life (Ehlers et al., 1987).
claims.evidence: This is observed in Figure 1B and compared to published mRNA half-life data from Ehlers et al., 1987.

claims.claim: Total VSG mRNA initially peaked at 180% but leveled to approximately wild-type quantities within 8 hr.
claims.source: The total VSG mRNA initially peaked at 180%, but within 8 hr leveled to approximately wild-type quantities.
claims.evidence: This is quantified from the data shown in Figure 1B.

claims.claim: The VSG mRNA population was effectively exchanged within 8 hr of VSG121 induction.
claims.source: Thus, the VSG mRNA population was effectively exchanged in this time period.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the kinetics data shown in Figure 1B.

claims.claim: VSG121 protein was detectable within 4–6 hr after induction.
claims.source: The VSG121 protein was detectable within 4–6 hr after induction (Figure 1B).
claims.evidence: This is measured experimental data shown in Figure 1B.

claims.claim: After 24 hr of VSG121 induction, the surface coat of all cells was dominated by VSG121.
claims.source: After 24 hr, the surface coat of all cells was dominated by VSG121 (Figure 1—figure supplement 1) and the amount of VSG221 had declined to 21(±2)% (Figure 1B).
claims.evidence: This is shown by immunofluorescence in Figure 1—figure supplement 1 and quantified in Figure 1B.

claims.claim: The amount of VSG221 declined to 21(±2)% after 24 hr of VSG121 induction.
claims.source: After 24 hr, the surface coat of all cells was dominated by VSG121 (Figure 1—figure supplement 1) and the amount of VSG221 had declined to 21(±2)% (Figure 1B).
claims.evidence: This is quantified from protein measurements shown in Figure 1B.

claims.claim: VSG221 decreased with a half-life of 12 hr corresponding to the population doubling time within the first 24 hr of induction.
claims.source: Thus, expression of an ectopic VSG at wild-type quantities caused a reduction in the abundance of the ES-resident VSG, which decreased with a half-life of 12 hr that corresponds to the population doubling time within the first 24 hr of induction.
claims.evidence: This is calculated from the data in Figure 1B and compared to growth data.

claims.claim: mRNAs from telomere proximal ESAG1 and 2 genes decreased faster than mRNA from telomere distal ESAG12 gene.
claims.source: It appears that mRNAs from the telomere proximal ESAG1 and 2 genes decreased faster than mRNA from the telomere distal ESAG12 gene.
claims.evidence: This is observed in the Northern blot data shown in Figure 2B.

claims.claim: Promoter proximal GFP mRNA decreased with significantly slower kinetics (p<0.018) than promoter distal GFP upon VSG121 induction.
claims.source: Upon induction of VSG121 expression, the promoter proximal GFP mRNA decreased with significantly slower kinetics (p<0.018; two-way ANOVA test) than that of the promoter distal GFP (Figure 2C, left panel), revealing that the kinetics of GFP mRNA reduction was determined solely by the position of the GFP gene within the active ES.
claims.evidence: This is measured experimental data with statistical analysis shown in Figure 2C.

claims.claim: The kinetics of GFP mRNA reduction was determined solely by the position of the GFP gene within the active ES.
claims.source: Upon induction of VSG121 expression, the promoter proximal GFP mRNA decreased with significantly slower kinetics (p<0.018; two-way ANOVA test) than that of the promoter distal GFP (Figure 2C, left panel), revealing that the kinetics of GFP mRNA reduction was determined solely by the position of the GFP gene within the active ES.
claims.evidence: This is concluded from the differential kinetics of GFP reporters at different positions shown in Figure 2C.

claims.claim: VSG121 overexpression caused a gradual loss of ES activity that started at the telomere and propagated towards the VSG promoter.
claims.source: Thus, VSG121 overexpression caused a gradual loss of ES activity that started at the telomere and propagated towards the VSG promoter.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the position-dependent kinetics of mRNA reduction shown in Figures 2B and 2C.

claims.claim: ES attenuation was completed within one cell division cycle.
claims.source: This process was completed within one cell division cycle and was maintained for 120 hr (Figure 1B).
claims.evidence: This is observed from the kinetics data in Figure 1B.

claims.claim: ES attenuation was maintained for 120 hr after VSG121 induction.
claims.source: This process was completed within one cell division cycle and was maintained for 120 hr (Figure 1B).
claims.evidence: This is observed from the time course data in Figure 1B.

claims.claim: The ES was gradually reactivated in the reverse direction after 120 hr.
claims.source: Then the ES was gradually reactivated in the reverse direction (Figure 2C).
claims.evidence: This is shown by the GFP reporter kinetics in Figure 2C.

claims.claim: The ES was not silenced completely, representing ES attenuation rather than bona fide ES silencing.
claims.source: The ES was not silenced completely, so the effect did not constitute a bona fide ES silencing, but a fine-tuned ES attenuation.
claims.evidence: This is concluded from the observation that ES activity decreased to ~20% but not to zero.

claims.claim: Parasite growth was not affected for the first 24 hr of VSG121 induction.
claims.source: The immediate early effect of VSG121 overexpression was the attenuation of the active ES (Figures 1 and 2). Parasite growth was not affected for the first 24 hr of tetracycline induction, but then cell proliferation slowed down significantly (Figure 3A).
claims.evidence: This is shown in the growth curve in Figure 3A.

claims.claim: Cell proliferation slowed down significantly after 24 hr of VSG121 induction.
claims.source: Parasite growth was not affected for the first 24 hr of tetracycline induction, but then cell proliferation slowed down significantly (Figure 3A).
claims.evidence: This is shown in the growth curve in Figure 3A.

claims.claim: Cell cycle analysis showed an accumulation of 1K1N cells with pre-replication kinetoplast morphology after VSG121 induction.
claims.source: The cell cycle was analyzed by determining the nucleus (N) and kinetoplast (K) configuration and showed an accumulation of 1K1N cells with the kinetoplasts having a pre-replication morphology and a reduction of cells containing a dividing kinetoplast (Figure 3B,C).
claims.evidence: This is shown by microscopy analysis in Figures 3B and 3C.

claims.claim: There was a reduction of cells containing a dividing kinetoplast after VSG121 induction.
claims.source: The cell cycle was analyzed by determining the nucleus (N) and kinetoplast (K) configuration and showed an accumulation of 1K1N cells with the kinetoplasts having a pre-replication morphology and a reduction of cells containing a dividing kinetoplast (Figure 3B,C).
claims.evidence: This is shown by cell cycle analysis in Figures 3B and 3C.

claims.claim: After 24 hr of VSG121 expression, only 17% of trypanosomes entered nuclear S-phase within a 4-hr labeling window.
claims.source: In the control (0 hr), 80% of trypanosomes had entered nuclear S-phase within the 4-hr labeling window. In contrast, after 24 hr of VSG121 expression only 17% incorporated EdU into nuclear DNA within an equivalent 4-hr window.
claims.evidence: This is measured by EdU incorporation shown in Figure 3D.

claims.claim: When parasites were incubated with EdU for 18 hr after 24 hr of VSG121 expression, 86% had entered S-phase.
claims.source: However, when the parasites were incubated with EdU for 18 hr, 86% had entered S-phase.
claims.evidence: This is measured by EdU incorporation shown in Figure 3D.

claims.claim: ES attenuation causes at least a fivefold expansion of the G1-phase from 3 to 15 hr.
claims.source: Thus, the cells were clearly not arrested in the cell cycle, but showed a specific, at least fivefold expansion of the G1-phase from 3 to 15 hr.
claims.evidence: This is calculated from the EdU incorporation data in Figure 3D.

claims.claim: All trypanosomes remained fully motile during ES attenuation.
claims.source: Remarkably, all trypanosomes remained fully motile and no morphological abnormality or cell death was observed.
claims.evidence: This is an observational finding from the experiments.

claims.claim: No morphological abnormality or cell death was observed during ES attenuation.
claims.source: Remarkably, all trypanosomes remained fully motile and no morphological abnormality or cell death was observed.
claims.evidence: This is an observational finding shown in Figure 3C.

claims.claim: After 8 hr of VSG121 induction, the general transcription rate was not impaired.
claims.source: After 8 hr of tetracycline induction, when VSG221 transcripts had already decreased to 20%, the general transcription rate was not impaired at all.
claims.evidence: This is measured by BrUTP incorporation shown in Figure 3E.

claims.claim: After 24 hr of VSG121 induction, global transcription was reduced to 30% (p<0.0001).
claims.source: Only after 24 hr was the global transcription reduced to 30% (p<0.0001; unpaired t test) (Figure 3E).
claims.evidence: This is measured by BrUTP incorporation with statistical analysis shown in Figure 3E.

claims.claim: ES attenuation precedes growth retardation and general transcriptional diminution.
claims.source: This formally proves that ES attenuation precedes growth retardation and general transcriptional diminution.
claims.evidence: This is concluded from the temporal sequence of events shown in Figures 1-3.

claims.claim: Both RNA polymerase I and II transcription were affected by ES attenuation.
claims.source: To test if RNA polymerase I and II transcription was both affected, we inserted luciferase reporter transgenes either downstream of an rDNA promoter or into the tubulin-locus (Figure 3—figure supplement 1). In both the cases, luciferase activity was down to 30–50% within 2 days.
claims.evidence: This is shown by luciferase reporter assays in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: Luciferase activity from both Pol I and Pol II promoters decreased to 30–50% within 2 days of VSG121 induction.
claims.source: To test if RNA polymerase I and II transcription was both affected, we inserted luciferase reporter transgenes either downstream of an rDNA promoter or into the tubulin-locus (Figure 3—figure supplement 1). In both the cases, luciferase activity was down to 30–50% within 2 days.
claims.evidence: This is measured by luciferase assays shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: DOT1B is involved in the silencing of the active ES during in situ switching.
claims.source: The histone methyltransferase DOT1B is involved in the silencing of the active ES during in situ switching (Figueiredo et al., 2008).
claims.evidence: This is cited from Figueiredo et al., 2008.

claims.claim: In DOT1B-deleted cells, VSG221 protein decreased with the same kinetics as in parental cells following VSG121 induction.
claims.source: Following induction of VSG121 expression, the decrease of the ES-resident VSG221 protein occurred with the same kinetics as in the parental cells (Figure 4A).
claims.evidence: This is shown by protein quantification in Figure 4A.

claims.claim: In DOT1B-deleted cells, VSG221 protein levels did not increase again after initial decrease.
claims.source: However, unlike in the parental cell line the protein levels did not increase again.
claims.evidence: This is shown by the time course in Figure 4A compared to Figure 1B.

claims.claim: DOT1B-deleted cells did not display a growth phenotype upon VSG121 induction.
claims.source: Furthermore, the cells did not display a growth phenotype (Figure 4B).
claims.evidence: This is shown by the growth curve in Figure 4B.

claims.claim: In DOT1B-knockout trypanosomes, luciferase activity was only marginally and transiently reduced at day 2.
claims.source: However, in the DOT1B-knockout trypanosomes luciferase activity was only marginally and transiently reduced at day 2 (Figure 4C, left panel).
claims.evidence: This is shown by luciferase assays in Figure 4C.

claims.claim: In DOT1B-deleted cells, the ES was not attenuated except for the most telomere-proximal part where the VSG221 gene resides.
claims.source: Thus, in DOT1B-deleted cells, the ES was not attenuated, except for the most telomere-proximal part, where the VSG221 gene resides.
claims.evidence: This is concluded from the luciferase data in Figure 4C showing differential effects at different ES positions.

claims.claim: Silencing of a VSG gene can be uncoupled from ES silencing.
claims.source: This suggests that silencing of a VSG gene can be uncoupled from ES silencing.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the DOT1B knockout data in Figure 4.

claims.claim: ES attenuation requires DOT1B-dependent histone tri-methylation.
claims.source: While ES attenuation seems to require DOT1B-dependent histone tri-methylation, VSG silencing does not.
claims.evidence: This is concluded from the differential effects in DOT1B knockout cells shown in Figure 4.

claims.claim: VSG silencing does not require DOT1B-dependent histone tri-methylation.
claims.source: While ES attenuation seems to require DOT1B-dependent histone tri-methylation, VSG silencing does not.
claims.evidence: This is concluded from the observation that VSG221 is silenced in DOT1B knockout cells shown in Figure 4A.

claims.claim: The ES-resident VSG can be complemented in trans by a heterologous VSG gene.
claims.source: Furthermore, these results formally prove that the ES-resident VSG can be complemented in trans by a heterologous VSG gene.
claims.evidence: This is concluded from the lack of growth phenotype in DOT1B knockout cells expressing ectopic VSG121.

claims.claim: High-level expression of a second VSG is sufficient to attenuate and eventually silence the formerly active ES.
claims.source: We conclude that the activation of a new VSG ES initiates an in situ switch, and that high-level expression of a second VSG is sufficient to attenuate and eventually silence the formerly active ES.
claims.evidence: This is the main conclusion from the experimental data in Figures 1-4.

claims.claim: A VSG-mediated feedback loop assures monoallelic expression of VSG.
claims.source: This feedback loop assures monoallelic expression of the VSG.
claims.evidence: This is concluded from the mechanism demonstrated in the experiments.

claims.claim: PAD1 protein was detectable on the surface of trypanosomes in G1-phase after 48 hr of VSG121 overexpression.
claims.source: After 48 hr of VSG121 overexpression, however, the PAD1 protein was clearly detectable on the surface of trypanosomes in the G1-phase of the cell cycle (Figure 5A,B).
claims.evidence: This is shown by immunofluorescence in Figure 5A and quantified in Figure 5B.

claims.claim: The GFP:PADutr reporter was visible in most G1 cells after 48 hr of VSG121 overexpression.
claims.source: Likewise, the GFP:PADutr reporter was visible in most G1 cells, but was also expressed in a minor portion of trypanosomes in other cell cycle phases (Figure 5C).
claims.evidence: This is shown by microscopy and flow cytometry in Figure 5C.

claims.claim: VSG overexpression-induced ES attenuation triggers G1-phase prolongation and expression of PAD1 in monomorphic slender stage trypanosomes.
claims.source: We conclude that in the absence of the quorum-sensing factor SIF and at 37°C, the VSG overexpression-induced ES attenuation triggers G1-phase prolongation and concomitant expression of a bona fide stumpy marker in monomorphic slender stage trypanosomes.
claims.evidence: This is concluded from the data in Figures 3 and 5.

claims.claim: PAD1 expression was induced despite global transcriptional attenuation.
claims.source: Notably, PAD1 expression was induced despite the global transcriptional attenuation that started at the same time.
claims.evidence: This is observed by comparing the timing of PAD1 induction (Figure 5) with global transcription reduction (Figure 3E).

claims.claim: ES-attenuated trypanosomes became fully responsive to cis-aconitate after 48 hr of VSG121 induction.
claims.source: We induced VSG121 expression for 48 hr and then incubated the trypanosomes in the absence of tetracycline with 6 mM cis-aconitate. Immunofluorescence analysis revealed EP1 surface expression as early as 6 hr after addition of cis-aconitate (Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
claims.evidence: This is shown by EP1 expression analysis in Figure 6 and Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: EP1 surface expression was detectable as early as 6 hr after addition of cis-aconitate to ES-attenuated cells.
claims.source: Immunofluorescence analysis revealed EP1 surface expression as early as 6 hr after addition of cis-aconitate (Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
claims.evidence: This is shown by immunofluorescence in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: After 24 hr of cis-aconitate treatment, 70(±6)% of ES-attenuated cells were EP1-positive.
claims.source: After 24 hr, 70(±6)% of cells were EP1-positive (Figure 6A,B).
claims.evidence: This is quantified by flow cytometry in Figure 6A,B.

claims.claim: ES-attenuated trypanosomes altered their cell architecture, adopting a stumpy-like morphology after 6 hr of cis-aconitate treatment.
claims.source: Furthermore, the trypanosomes also altered their cell architecture, adopting a stumpy-like morphology after 6 hr of cis-aconitate treatment.
claims.evidence: This is shown by microscopy in Figure 6C and Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: After 24 hr of cis-aconitate treatment, the posterior part of ES-attenuated cells had elongated and the kinetoplast had repositioned and segregated.
claims.source: After 24 hr, the posterior part of the cells had elongated and the kinetoplast had repositioned and segregated (Figure 6C, Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
claims.evidence: This is shown by microscopy in Figure 6C and Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: After 6 hr of cis-aconitate treatment at 27°C, 58(±8)% of ES-attenuated cells revealed strong EP1 fluorescence on the cell surface.
claims.source: After 6 hr, 58(±8)% of cells revealed strong EP1 fluorescence on the cell surface, while only 5(±2)% of the control population were EP1-positive (Figure 6D,E).
claims.evidence: This is quantified by flow cytometry in Figure 6D,E.

claims.claim: Only 5(±2)% of control cells were EP1-positive after 6 hr of cis-aconitate treatment at 27°C.
claims.source: After 6 hr, 58(±8)% of cells revealed strong EP1 fluorescence on the cell surface, while only 5(±2)% of the control population were EP1-positive (Figure 6D,E).
claims.evidence: This is quantified by flow cytometry in Figure 6D,E.

claims.claim: ES-attenuated trypanosomes accelerated the cell cycle after 24 hr at 27°C and started growing as procyclic trypanosomes.
claims.source: Interestingly, the ES-attenuated trypanosomes accelerated the cell cycle after 24 hr and started growing as procyclic trypanosomes (Figure 6F).
claims.evidence: This is shown by growth curves in Figure 6F.

claims.claim: VSG-induced ES attenuation triggers cell biological reprogramming of the parasite and causes gain of full developmental competence.
claims.source: We conclude that the VSG-induced ES attenuation triggers the cell biological reprogramming of the parasite and causes the concomitant gain of full developmental competence.
claims.evidence: This is concluded from the differentiation experiments shown in Figures 5 and 6.

claims.claim: ESAG1-RNAi reduced transcript levels to 30%.

claims.claim: ESAG2-RNAi reduced mRNA to less than 5%.

claims.evidence: This is shown by growth curves in Figure 7A.

claims.claim: ESAG2-RNAi caused the fraction of GFP-positive cells to increase twofold in the first 24 hr.

claims.evidence: This is shown by flow cytometry in Figure 7D.

claims.claim: After 3 days of ESAG2-RNAi, GFP was detected in 75% of all cells.

claims.evidence: This is shown by flow cytometry in Figure 7D.

claims.claim: After 3 days of ESAG2-RNAi, cell growth stopped and parasites started to die.

claims.evidence: This is shown by growth curves in Figure 7C.

claims.claim: Only ablation of ESAGs 1, 2, and 8 induced PAD1 expression.

claims.claim: Down-regulation of ESAGs 3, 6, 7, and 12 was not accompanied by PAD1 expression.

claims.evidence: This is shown by flow cytometry in Figure 7—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: G1-retardation and PAD1 expression is caused by the depletion of three ESAGs (1, 2, and 8).
claims.source: These results strongly suggest that G1-retardation and PAD1 expression is caused by the depletion of three ESAGs.
claims.evidence: This is concluded from the RNAi experiments in Figure 7 and Figure 7—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: Loss of ESAG homeostasis is an immediate early signal for developmental stage transition.
claims.source: Thus, loss of ESAG homeostasis is an immediate early signal for developmental stage transition.
claims.evidence: This is concluded from the ESAG RNAi experiments showing PAD1 induction.

claims.claim: Starting at day 5 of VSG121 induction, the attenuation of the VSG221 ES was gradually lifted.
claims.source: Starting at day 5 of VSG121 induction, the attenuation of the VSG221 ES was gradually lifted.
claims.evidence: This is shown by the kinetics data in Figure 2C.

claims.claim: The kinetics of ES re-activation was directional, starting at the promoter and proceeding towards the telomere.
claims.source: Interestingly, the kinetics of ES re-activation was also directional, starting at the promoter and proceeding towards the telomere.
claims.evidence: This is shown by the GFP reporter kinetics in Figure 2C.

claims.claim: VSG221 mRNA slowly increased to pre-induction levels between days 5 and 8.
claims.source: VSG221 mRNA slowly increased to pre-induction levels between days 5 and 8 (Figure 1B).
claims.evidence: This is shown by mRNA quantification in Figure 1B.

claims.claim: At day 8, the VSG221 surface coat had returned and VSG121 was back to pre-induction levels.

results.result: African trypanosomes possess hundreds of VSG genes, but only one is expressed from a telomeric expression site (ES) at any given time.
results.evaluation: Claims C1, C2, C17, and C18 establish the fundamental biology of VSG expression in trypanosomes. These are well-established facts supported by multiple citations (Berriman et al., 2005; Hertz-Fowler et al., 2008) and represent accepted knowledge in the field.

results.result: Expression of a second VSG (VSG121) at wild-type levels causes rapid exchange of VSG mRNA and protein, with VSG221 declining to 21% within 24 hours.
results.evaluation: Claims C3 and C27-C34 describe the kinetics of VSG exchange following induction of ectopic VSG121. The data in Figure 1B provide quantitative measurements of mRNA and protein levels over time, showing VSG121 mRNA reaching 82±1% within 2 hours and VSG221 protein declining to 21±2% by 24 hours. The measurements are well-documented with error bars and multiple time points.

results.result: VSG overexpression causes directional ES attenuation that starts at the telomere and propagates toward the promoter, reducing ES activity to ~20% but not completely silencing it.
results.evaluation: Claims C4 and C35-C42 describe the directional nature of ES attenuation. The position-dependent kinetics are demonstrated using GFP reporters at different ES positions (Figure 2C), with statistical significance (p<0.018, two-way ANOVA). The observation that ES activity decreases to ~20% rather than zero is consistently shown across multiple experiments and is a key distinction made by the authors.

results.result: ES attenuation causes specific G1-phase prolongation (at least fivefold, from 3 to 15 hours) without cell cycle arrest, with cells remaining motile and morphologically normal.
results.evaluation: Claims C43-C51 describe the cell cycle effects of ES attenuation. The data are supported by multiple complementary approaches: growth curves (Figure 3A), cell cycle analysis by K/N configuration (Figures 3B,C), and EdU incorporation experiments (Figure 3D). The fivefold expansion calculation is based on comparing 17% vs 80% S-phase entry in 4 hours, and 86% entry in 18 hours, which is internally consistent.

results.result: ES attenuation precedes global transcriptional diminution, with general transcription unaffected at 8 hours but reduced to 30% by 24 hours, affecting both Pol I and Pol II transcription.
results.evaluation: Claims C52-C56 establish the temporal relationship between ES attenuation and global transcription. BrUTP incorporation data (Figure 3E) show no change at 8 hours but significant reduction (p<0.0001) to 30% at 24 hours. Luciferase reporters driven by both Pol I (rDNA) and Pol II (tubulin) promoters show similar 30-50% reduction (Figure 3—figure supplement 1), supporting the claim that both polymerases are affected.

results.result: ES attenuation requires DOT1B-dependent histone methylation, but VSG silencing does not; in DOT1B knockout cells, VSG221 is silenced without ES attenuation or growth phenotype.
results.evaluation: Claims C57-C68 describe the role of DOT1B in ES attenuation. The experiments in Figure 4 show that in DOT1B knockout cells, VSG221 protein decreases with the same kinetics as wild-type (C58), but the ES is not attenuated except at the telomere-proximal VSG locus (C62), and there is no growth phenotype (C60). This mechanistic separation of VSG silencing from ES attenuation is well-supported by the luciferase reporter data (Figure 4C).

results.result: Three specific ESAGs (1, 2, and 8) signal ES attenuation to cause G1-phase dormancy and PAD1 expression; depletion of other ESAGs does not induce PAD1.
results.evaluation: Claims C5-C7 and C82-C93 describe the role of specific ESAGs in signaling ES attenuation. RNAi experiments (Figure 7 and Figure 7—figure supplement 1) show that only depletion of ESAGs 1, 2, and 8 induces PAD1 expression, while depletion of ESAGs 3, 6, 7, and 12 does not. The specificity is well-documented with growth curves and flow cytometry data. However, the claim that ESAG1 RNAi reduced transcripts to only 30% (C82) while ESAG2 RNAi reduced to <5% (C83) raises questions about whether the ESAG1 phenotype might be underestimated due to incomplete knockdown.

results.result: ES attenuation triggers PAD1 expression specifically in G1-phase cells after 48 hours, despite global transcriptional attenuation, in the absence of the quorum-sensing factor SIF.
results.evaluation: Claims C69-C72 and C143-C144 describe PAD1 induction following ES attenuation. The data in Figure 5 show PAD1 protein on the cell surface and GFP:PADutr reporter expression predominantly in G1 cells after 48 hours of VSG121 induction. The cell cycle specificity is quantified (Figure 5B,C) with statistical significance. The observation that PAD1 is induced despite global transcriptional attenuation (which starts at 24 hours) is temporally consistent with the data.

results.result: ES-attenuated trypanosomes gain full developmental competence for transformation to the procyclic insect stage, responding to cis-aconitate with EP1 expression and morphological changes characteristic of differentiation.
results.evaluation: Claims C8 and C73-C81 describe the developmental competence gained by ES-attenuated cells. The experiments in Figure 6 demonstrate EP1 surface expression (70±6% at 24 hours at 37°C, 58±8% at 6 hours at 27°C) and morphological changes following cis-aconitate treatment. The kinetics are comparable to stumpy parasites, and the cells can grow as procyclics at 27°C (Figure 6F). The data are comprehensive and include appropriate controls.

results.result: ES attenuation is fully reversible, with the ES reactivating directionally from promoter to telomere starting at day 5, and cells returning to normal growth by day 10; all 20 clonal populations reactivated the original ES without switching.
results.evaluation: Claims C94-C102 and C152-C153 describe the reversibility of ES attenuation. The data in Figures 1B, 2C, and 3A show temporal progression of ES reactivation and return to normal growth. The claim that all 20 clones reactivated the VSG221 ES (C100) is stated but not shown in detail. The observation that >20% of cells respond to re-induction after 10 days (C101) argues against selection of revertants, though this percentage seems relatively low and might warrant further investigation.

results.result: The VSG expression site functions as a fine-tuned regulator linking antigenic variation, cell proliferation, and developmental competence through VSG-mediated feedback and ESAG-dependent signaling.
results.evaluation: Claims C103-C105 and C109 represent the main conceptual conclusions of the study. These are well-supported by the collective experimental evidence showing: (1) VSG-mediated ES attenuation (Figures 1-2), (2) ESAG-dependent effects on cell cycle and PAD1 expression (Figures 3, 5, 7), and (3) developmental competence (Figure 6). The integration of these findings into a unified model is logical and supported by the data.

results.result: The mechanistic principle of feedback inhibition in monoallelic expression appears conserved between the trypanosome VSG system and the mammalian olfactory receptor system, despite evolutionary distance.
results.evaluation: Claims C9-C12 and C106-C108 draw parallels between the VSG and OR systems. While the comparison is conceptually interesting and both systems show feedback inhibition by the expressed gene product, the claim of conservation (C107) is speculative. The mechanisms may be analogous rather than homologous, and the authors acknowledge key differences (C108). The comparison is useful for framing but lacks direct experimental evidence for mechanistic conservation.

results.result: The experimental system initiates but does not complete VSG switching because it lacks functional ESAGs; cells respond by attenuating ES activity to ~20% and entering a semi-quiescent state that is reversible after ~5 days.
results.evaluation: Claims C110-C122 interpret the experimental observations in the context of natural VSG switching. The interpretation that the system initiates but cannot complete switching (C111) is reasonable given that the ectopic VSG121 is not in an ES and lacks ESAGs. The observation of ~20% residual ES activity (C112, C117) is consistent across experiments. The differential effects of ESAG1 vs ESAG2 depletion (C119-C122) are well-documented in Figure 7.

results.result: Transient ES attenuation may allow parasites to probe ES performance and adapt to new conditions or reverse attenuation, with ES switching plasticity potentially determining host range.
results.evaluation: Claims C128-C133 are speculative models proposed by the authors to explain the biological significance of ES attenuation. While these are plausible hypotheses consistent with the experimental observations, they lack direct experimental support. The ideas about probing ES performance (C128), unsuccessful switching events (C132), and host range determination (C133) are interesting but remain to be tested.

results.result: T. b. rhodesiense may have lost ESAGs 1, 2, and 8 from its SRA-containing ES to prevent ES switching that would cause loss of human infectivity.
results.evaluation: Claims C134-C139 present an evolutionary hypothesis about T. b. rhodesiense. While the facts about T. b. rhodesiense being human-infective (C134-C135) and having an unusual ES structure (C136) are established knowledge, the speculation that this ES has lost ESAGs 1, 2, and 8 (C139) to prevent the ESAG-dependent differentiation pathway (C138) is not directly tested. This is an interesting hypothesis but requires experimental validation.

results.result: VSG-induced ES attenuation can render monomorphic cells developmentally competent, and preliminary data suggest this also occurs in pleomorphic strains leading to stumpy formation.
results.evaluation: Claims C140-C142 are well-supported by the data in Figure 6 showing that monomorphic cells gain developmental competence. However, claim C145 about stumpy formation in pleomorphic strains is stated as unpublished data ('data not shown'), which cannot be evaluated. This is an important claim that requires full documentation to be considered supported.

results.result: ES-attenuated parasites differ from SIF-induced stumpy forms in that differentiation is reversible rather than terminal, and cells can complete ES switching by adapting to a new ES.
results.evaluation: Claims C151-C154 distinguish ES attenuation from SIF-mediated stumpy formation. The reversibility is well-documented in Figures 1-3 showing ES reactivation and return to normal growth. The claim about completing ES switching (C154) is more speculative, as the experimental system doesn't actually demonstrate successful completion of a natural ES switch, but the logic is sound based on the observed flexibility.

results.result: Prior to this study, no mechanism for initiating in situ ES switching had been identified, and ES silencing accompanies developmental transitions in the trypanosome life cycle.
results.evaluation: Claims C19-C26 establish the background knowledge and novelty of the study. These are well-supported by appropriate citations and represent accepted understanding in the field. Claim C22 correctly identifies the gap in knowledge that this study addresses.

results.result: Antigenic variation through monoallelic VSG expression is a key survival strategy in trypanosomes and other pathogens like Plasmodium falciparum.
results.evaluation: Claims C13-C16 provide background on antigenic variation in pathogens. These are well-established facts supported by appropriate citations and represent foundational knowledge for understanding the significance of the study.

results.result: ESAGs 1 and 2 are membrane-associated proteins that may function in the endosome pathway, while ESAG8 is found in the nucleolus/cytoplasm and may be linked to mRNA regulation and differentiation.
results.evaluation: Claims C123-C127 describe known properties of ESAGs based on prior literature. While the localizations (C123, C125) and interactions (C126) are cited from published work, the functional interpretations (C124, C127) are speculative ('suggested', 'may play a role'). These provide useful context but don't constitute new findings from this study.

results.result: Expression of ectopic VSG121 leads to rapid silencing of the endogenous VSG221 gene. VSG121 mRNA reached 82% of wild-type levels within 2 hours, followed by decline of VSG221 transcripts with kinetics compatible with mRNA half-life. Total VSG mRNA peaked at 180% but leveled to wild-type quantities within 8 hours, with VSG121 protein detectable within 4-6 hours and dominating the surface coat by 24 hours.
results.evaluation: Reviewers raised major concerns about whether this experimental system truly mimics physiological VSG switching or represents a toxic artifact. They questioned whether 'the observed return to growth after 5 days, associated with re-expression of VSG221...could represent the selection for revertants that suppress ectopic expression of VSG121' and noted that 'these data might also be explained by over-expression of VSG121 being toxic to the cells.' The reviewers requested clarification on whether VSG121 can be re-induced after reversion, stating 'we are provided with no evidence to support the putative claim that VSG121 can be re-induced at this stage.'

results.result: ES attenuation proceeds directionally from telomere to promoter. Telomere-proximal ESAG mRNAs decreased faster than promoter-distal ones, with position-dependent kinetics demonstrated by GFP reporters. The process was completed within one cell division cycle, maintained for 120 hours, then gradually reversed. ES activity decreased to ~20% rather than complete silencing.
results.evaluation: While reviewers did not directly challenge the directional attenuation data, they expressed concern about the physiological relevance of the entire experimental system. The concern that the system may not mimic true VSG switching (as noted in their comment that 'it seems that the only circumstances in which ESAGs are not co-expressed with the VSG is when an ES is activated that lacks these genes') casts doubt on whether this directional attenuation represents a genuine biological mechanism or an artifact of ectopic VSG expression.

results.result: VSG121 induction causes G1-phase expansion and growth retardation. Growth was unaffected for 24 hours but then slowed significantly, with accumulation of 1K1N cells and fivefold expansion of G1-phase from 3 to 15 hours. Cells remained motile with no morphological abnormalities or death.
results.evaluation: Reviewers questioned whether these phenotypes reflect physiological processes or toxicity, stating 'the growth, replication and gene expression effects that are observed might be explained by the cells becoming very sick upon VSG121 induction' and suggesting 'very high levels of mRNA for VSG121, or perhaps very high levels of two VSGs, overwhelm the transcription and translation apparatus of the cell.' This fundamental concern about the experimental system undermines confidence in the biological significance of the growth phenotype.

results.result: Global transcription is reduced following ES attenuation. General transcription was unimpaired at 8 hours but reduced to 30% by 24 hours (p<0.0001), affecting both RNA polymerase I and II transcription. ES attenuation precedes this general transcriptional diminution.
results.evaluation: Reviewers explicitly challenged this finding, noting that 'in more recent work, using whole-genome gene expression analyses (Kabani et al, 2009; Capewell et al, 2013), there is little evidence for such global reduction in transcription' during stumpy differentiation. They stated 'the global effects described here upon VSG121 induction may not reflect the developmental change from long slender to short stumpy cells, but instead toxic effects of VSG121 overexpression.' This directly contradicts the authors' interpretation that global transcription reduction is a physiological consequence of ES attenuation.

results.result: ES attenuation requires DOT1B-mediated histone methylation, but VSG silencing does not. In DOT1B-deleted cells, VSG221 protein decreased with the same kinetics but did not increase again, cells showed no growth phenotype, and the ES was not attenuated except at the telomere-proximal VSG locus. This demonstrates that VSG silencing can be uncoupled from ES silencing.
results.evaluation: Reviewers did not raise specific concerns about the DOT1B experiments or their interpretation. The data showing differential effects in DOT1B knockout cells appears to have been accepted as demonstrating a mechanistic distinction between VSG silencing and broader ES attenuation, though the overall physiological relevance remains questioned.

results.result: High-level expression of a second VSG is sufficient to attenuate the formerly active ES through a VSG-mediated feedback loop that assures monoallelic expression. This feedback mechanism controls the state of monoallelic gene expression.
results.evaluation: Reviewers strongly challenged this model, noting that 'this model predicts that two VSGs cannot be simultaneously expressed, as one will trigger suppression of another. However, double VSG expressers have been reported...and do not impair growth: Baltz et al. (1986); Munoz-Jordan et al. (1996).' They also questioned how this could work physiologically since 'in the normal context a second VSG can only be expressed in conjunction with the upstream ESAGs, since they share a common promoter in the ES.' The editors requested further clarification, asking 'Would the model not predict attenuation of the downstream VSG in the experiments reported by Munoz-Jordan et al. (1996)?'

results.result: Three ESAGs (1, 2, and 8) serve as signals for ES attenuation and developmental transition. RNAi depletion of these ESAGs causes G1-phase dormancy and reversible initiation of differentiation with PAD1 expression, while depletion of other ESAGs does not induce PAD1. Loss of ESAG homeostasis is an immediate early signal for developmental stage transition.
results.evaluation: Reviewers expressed concern about the specificity and mechanism, noting 'it's difficult to see how each gene knockdown acts redundantly to bring about this effect' and requesting 'more about the putative functions of these ESAGs relative to those not linked to this phenotype.' They also noted that 'ESAG 5, present in all known ES was not tested' and that 'the data would be strengthened if ESAG5 RNAi was included.' The editors ultimately requested that the abstract be modified to state these ESAGs 'appear to serve' or 'could serve' as signals, acknowledging the speculative nature of this conclusion 'in the absence of knowing the functions of ESAGs 1, 2 and 8.'

results.result: ES attenuation triggers expression of the stumpy marker PAD1 in monomorphic slender trypanosomes. PAD1 protein was detectable on G1-phase cells after 48 hours of VSG121 overexpression, specifically in G1 cells, despite global transcriptional attenuation occurring simultaneously. This represents a highly specific event orchestrated by the state of the VSG expression site in the absence of SIF.
results.evaluation: While reviewers did not directly challenge the PAD1 expression data, their broader concerns about whether the experimental system mimics physiological processes apply here. The claim that this is 'orchestrated solely by the state of the VSG expression site' is undermined by reviewer concerns about the non-physiological nature of ectopic VSG expression and the question of whether effects represent toxicity rather than genuine developmental signaling.

results.result: ES-attenuated slender trypanosomes gain full developmental competence for transformation to procyclic forms. After 48 hours of VSG121 induction, cells became fully responsive to cis-aconitate, with EP1 expression detectable at 6 hours and 70% of cells EP1-positive by 24 hours. Cells adopted stumpy-like morphology and initiated transformation with the same kinetics as stumpy parasites.
results.evaluation: Reviewers did not raise specific concerns about the differentiation competence experiments. The data showing that ES-attenuated cells can respond to cis-aconitate and express procyclic markers appears to have been accepted. However, the broader interpretation of what this means for the physiological role of ES attenuation remains uncertain given concerns about the experimental system.

results.result: ES attenuation and its phenotypic consequences are fully reversible. Starting at day 5, the VSG221 ES was gradually reactivated in a directional manner from promoter to telomere, with VSG221 mRNA returning to pre-induction levels by day 8. G1-retardation was lifted and growth returned to normal by day 10. All 20 clonal populations reactivated the VSG221 ES with no ES switching, and cells remained responsive to VSG121 re-induction.
results.evaluation: Reviewers expressed significant concern about this reversibility, questioning whether it represents 'selection for revertants that suppress ectopic expression of VSG121.' They noted the authors' claim that cells 'became responsive to re-introduction of tetracycline' but stated 'the wording used is rather vague, and it is not at all clear whether this is their meaning' and 'we are provided with no evidence to support the putative claim that VSG121 can be re-induced at this stage.' They concluded 'if revertants are being selected for that no longer express VSG121, it suggests significant problems with the experimental approach.'

results.result: The ES functions as a fine-tuned regulator linking antigenic variation, proliferation, and development. Transcriptional activity of the ES directly determines cell proliferation and developmental competence via ESAGs, positioning the ES at the crossroads of these three key processes.
results.evaluation: Reviewers explicitly stated 'It is currently not convincing that the VSG expression site is a global regulator (end of the Introduction) or global control module (end of the Discussion) of antigenic variation, proliferation and development. Without studies in a fully differentiation-competent pleomorphic strain, strong conclusions can't be drawn. These sections should be toned down to reflect the uncertainty.' This directly challenges the authors' overarching model and conclusions.

results.result: The mechanistic principle of feedback inhibition in monoallelic expression appears conserved between the trypanosome VSG system and the mammalian olfactory receptor system, despite evolutionary distance. However, in trypanosomes an array of genes is attenuated whereas in the OR system only the receptor is silenced.
results.evaluation: This comparison is undermined by reviewers' challenge to the feedback model itself. Since reviewers questioned whether VSG expression truly triggers feedback inhibition (citing stable double VSG expressers), the claimed parallel with the OR system lacks support. The reviewers' concerns about the model predicting that 'two VSGs cannot be simultaneously expressed' directly contradicts the proposed conservation of mechanism.

results.result: The experimental system initiates but does not complete VSG switching because it lacks functional ESAGs. Cells respond by attenuating ES activity to ~20% rather than fully silencing it, entering a semi-quiescent state for ~5 days before resuming growth. This transient attenuation may allow probing for ES performance and functionality.
results.evaluation: These interpretations are speculative and built on the foundation of the experimental system whose physiological relevance reviewers questioned. The model that incomplete switching leads to attenuation rather than full silencing is challenged by reviewers' concern that 'in the normal context a second VSG can only be expressed in conjunction with the upstream ESAGs' and their question about whether the observed phenotypes represent artifacts of the non-physiological expression system.

results.result: ES switching plasticity could determine host range, exemplified by T. b. rhodesiense which must maintain expression of the SRA-containing ES for human infectivity. The unusual structure of this ES, lacking ESAGs 1, 2, and 8, may prevent ES switching and make the ESAG-dependent differentiation pathway obsolete.
results.evaluation: This is presented as speculation about host range determination. While reviewers did not specifically address this section, their broader concerns about the physiological relevance of the ES attenuation mechanism and the role of ESAGs undermine confidence in these extrapolations to host range and T. b. rhodesiense biology.

results.result: Background and established knowledge about VSG expression, antigenic variation, trypanosome development, monoallelic expression systems in other organisms, and ESAG properties.
results.evaluation: These claims represent established knowledge cited from the literature and were not challenged by reviewers. They provide context for the experimental work.
